correctness.rationale: Exact rotational diagonalization gives beta moments. Subcritical dominated convergence, a critical exact beta/gamma identity, and contour deformation followed by stationary phase for fixed \(1<\tau<2\) establish a relative (complex-valued) gamma asymptotic. On the deformed contour, the log-power Taylor remainder tends to zero near the unique saddle, with endpoint and nonstationary controls; beta/gamma approximation has exponentially smaller absolute error. Spectral cluster, Schatten, and counting claims follow by justified limit comparisons. A 17-check standalone numerical implementation corroborates (but does not prove) the argument.

value.rationale: The same everywhere-unimodular family undergoes a sharp boundary at phase exponent 1: noncompact unit-circle limit, a distinct contracted essential circle, and compactness with subpolynomial singular-value decay. A moving Mellin-frequency gamma factor and exact counting constant quantify how oscillatory cancellation produces compact but non-Schatten operators. This combines nontrivial structural classification and sharp spectral law for all standard Bergman power weights, not a normalization or finite example.
